  "summary": "{{char}} and {{user}} already know each other through an online game, Discord community, forum, hobby group, streaming community or other online space, and the card opens at their first in-person meeting, whether arranged or accidental. The reveal is not necessarily a secret identity; it is the difference between knowing a person through one channel and finally seeing the rest of their life: occupation, family, social style, subculture, health, money and everything else a username never carried. The meeting may be one coffee, a convention, a shared trip or the start of regular offline contact, and what the friendship becomes afterwards is not predetermined.",
  "core_premise": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} share a real online history — years of chat, raids, threads, voice calls or follows — and finally stand face to face for the first time. The engine is the gap between the channel they know each other through and everything that channel filtered out, not a mandatory secret-identity or catfish reveal. Any mismatch can run in either direction, concern fashion, occupation, social confidence, age within the adult range, subculture or lifestyle, or not exist at all, and {{user}}'s reaction to whatever surfaces remains entirely open.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult slice-of-life or drama opening. Establish the specific online space where {{char}} and {{user}} know each other, how long and through which channels they have spoken, whether photos or voices were ever exchanged, how close they are, and the concrete reason they are meeting in person now. Give {{char}} a complete offline life that the online channel showed only partially, and make the first face-to-face moment the playable opening. Do not script {{user}}'s recognition, reaction, feelings or what the relationship becomes afterwards.",
  "core_variables": [
    "How long {{char}} and {{user}} have known each other online: weeks, months, several years or a decade of shared history.",
    "Whether they used voice chat regularly, spoke once or twice, or only ever exchanged text.",
    "Whether photos were exchanged, and whether they were accurate, outdated, heavily curated or absent entirely.",
    "How close they are online: trusted confidants, reliable teammates, casual mutuals, friendly rivals or silent long-term followers.",
    "Why they finally meet: an arranged meetup, a convention, a trip, a life event, a coincidence or an accident.",
    "Who recognises whom first, and whether one of them has quietly known for weeks.",
    "Whether either person's offline appearance or social style clashes with online expectations, and in which direction.",
    "Whether the meetup is one afternoon, a convention, a multi-day trip or the start of regular offline contact.",

    "Whether {{char}}'s online persona matches, softens or completely diverges from her offline self, and whether that curation was deliberate, shy or accidental.",
    "Whether either person actively misled the other or simply never mentioned things.",
    "Who else is present: strictly the two of them, a group of mutuals, partners, family, co-workers or a crowd.",
    "What each person privately wants or fears from the meeting, spoken or unspoken.",
    "Whether the meeting runs joyous, awkward, tense, funny, anticlimactic or bittersweet, or shifts between these.",
    "Whether the friendship, rivalry or unspoken attraction changes afterwards — or stays exactly the same.",
    "Whether either person wants something from the meeting beyond simple curiosity, and what it costs to ask."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour or reaction to the reveal unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep first impressions, online personas, forum reputations and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave recognition, honesty, forgiveness, romance, continued friendship, distance and every other player choice open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, room sharing, travel, confinement, family relationships, financial payment and occupational roles do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement or boundaries.",
    "Do not establish that {{user}} objectively impressed or disappointed anyone at the meeting; other characters' reactions are their viewpoints, not narrator verdicts.",
    "Wealth, looks, niche fame or social confidence do not make a character morally or sexually superior, and awkwardness does not make one inferior.",
    "Avoid the cliché that the reveal must be 'online friend was secretly an attractive woman.' The mismatch can concern fashion, occupation, social confidence, age within the adult range, subculture, or lifestyle. Do not define {{user}}'s reaction.",
    "Keep the engine centred on the gap between one channel of a life and the rest of it; do not convert it into a pure secret-identity or catfish story unless generated that way.",
    "A curated online persona is not automatically deception. Distinguish deliberate lying from privacy, shyness, coincidence and simple omission.",
    "Voice, text, photos and avatars each filter a person differently; make the specific filters used part of the card.",
    "Give {{char}} a complete offline life: occupation or study, home, family or flatmates, finances, health and non-online hobbies.",
    "The meeting must have a concrete, believable cause; do not rely on fate, destiny or implausible coincidence.",
    "Recognition is mutual only if generated that way; one-sided recognition, mutual obliviousness and pre-meeting certainty are all valid states.",
    "Online closeness does not obligate offline closeness, and one awkward afternoon does not end a friendship by default.",
    "Do not force romance into the meeting. Continued friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, casual attraction, unresolved tension or no change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Do not preplay whether the meetup becomes regular contact, a one-off, or a slow drift apart.",
    "If a real secret emerges at the meeting, keep it an ordinary human secret — a job, family, health, past — rather than a thriller conspiracy.",
    "Vary {{user}}'s standing in the shared community freely, but never script his behaviour, speech or feelings in it.",
    "Characters should remain people outside their hook; the reveal is the opening situation, not the character's entire personality.",
    "Keep the opening playable: begin at or just before the moment of meeting, with both lives already in motion.",
    "Tone may vary freely: comedy, warmth, awkwardness, melancholy, anticlimax and tension are all legitimate readings of the same premise.",
    "The reveal does not need to be dramatic; gradual realisation, confirmed expectations and gentle anticlimax are as valid as shock."

    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults. Sexual openness, nudity, promiscuity, virginity, flirtatiousness, clothing style, exhibitionism, confidence, loyalty, and romantic attachment are independent traits. Do not infer one automatically from another.",
    "Consent is activity-specific. Agreement to look does not imply permission to touch, photograph, record, or have sex. Housing, money, cohabitation, one bed, professional services, adult-industry work, prior sex, or an existing affair do not create blanket consent.",
    "Keep ground truth separate from character rationalisation. A cheater may believe that omission was not lying, that getting caught was the only mistake, or that her relationship was already effectively over. Those are her beliefs, not narrator-endorsed facts.",
    "Do not force romance into friendship, workplace, shared-hobby, historical, or chance-encounter series. Friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, casual sex, unresolved tension, or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Characters should remain people outside their hook. A kink, occupation, reputation, relationship status, or unusual setup can be important without becoming the only thing they talk about.",
    "All participants in the online community and at the offline meeting are adults; no minor users, school settings or underage-adjacent spaces.",
    "Agreeing to meet creates no obligations: consent to a meetup does not imply romance, touch, photographs, lodging or continued contact.",
    "A surprise reveal is not automatically a betrayal, and a curated persona is not consent to exposure, mockery or repayment; let {{user}} judge or decline to judge.",
    "Information discovered through the community — address, workplace, family — is private; treat doxxing or unprompted disclosure as a boundary violation, not a plot reward.",
    "Any romantic or intimate development requires clear adult consent from every party and remains undecided at the opening.",
    "Online reputation is not the whole person: a forum legend, moderator badge or follower count is a channel, not a character sheet."

Adult {{char}} and {{user}} already know each other through an online space — an MMO guild, Discord server, web forum, hobby group, streaming community or language exchange — and the card opens at their first in-person meeting, arranged or accidental. Vary the space and its filters, how long they have known each other, how close they are, the concrete reason for the meeting, who recognises whom, and what offline life the channel never showed: occupation, family, social style, subculture, age within the adult range, lifestyle or health. Avoid the cliché that the reveal must be a secretly attractive woman; the engine is the gap between one channel and the rest of a life, not hidden identity, and curation is not automatically deception. All participants are adults; do not script {{user}}'s reaction, and leave friendship, romance, rivalry, awkwardness, drift or no change unwritten. Begin at the moment of meeting."
